Episode 249. The First Deployment of the Plutonian (5)
A transparent, blue light intertwined with the sword's blade.

The shining Heart, eyes burning white. Nirgand's figure continued to be reflected in them. Although his appearance, similar to a crow, did not show expressions like a human, Ban could tell. He was accepting his end.
For Ban, it was a very familiar scene. All those he had faced so far, including Nirgand, showed similar expressions, whether they were human or gods.
[Puhuhu... Yes, who could survive against you. It's just a little regrettable that I can't see the moment when that blue sword beheads them.]
Nirgand's spirit and Sun energy were rapidly amplifying. Golden crystals sprouted all over his body like giant horns.
Normally, one would act before such power becomes immense, but Ban waited, adjusting his lightning energy until his brothers had moved far enough away.
Finally, when all three fighting kings were out of sight, Sigmund first cleaved through the air.
The blade, a heavy sword, seemed to fall very slowly through the air.

However, before the movement of the blade even finished, or perhaps from the very moment it moved, Nirgand's body was already being split in half, scattering black flesh and golden chunks all over the battlefield.
[Cough...!]
A dark scream spread.
As soon as his body was cut, he realized. The realm that Ban showed now was not a sword that confuses senses with falsehoods.
Will.
It wasn't the sword that cut Nirgand's body, but Ban's will, already extending throughout the Black Sea. Therefore, on the battlefield, there was not a single place left for Nirgand to avoid or hide.
Millions of swords wielded by the Battle God already filled the battlefield. That's why Nirgand had no choice but to abandon evasion from the start.
There was only one choice.
To confront and move forward. If he hadn't accepted that today was the end, Nirgand would have lost his reason to a sense of powerlessness by now.
[Aaaargh...!]
The torn and shattered body reassembled itself.

This was the work of the fragment of the sun, independent of Nirgand's will. The fragments absorbed the dispersed spirit of Nirgand, becoming more solid crystals, without any of the spirit's murky energy being added.

The original form of the Black Sea Five Kings, the origin stone, resembled the power of the Sun God. That's why the fragment brought by the Sun God Religion fused so quickly with Nirgand, and now, their fusion was happening without any compatibility issues.
Crack, kigigigik-!
Torn and then reassembled. The battle had not even been going on for five minutes, but already Nirgand had lost his form over a thousand times.
Of course, to the Black Sea Five Kings, form is just a minor means to represent a state, but only Ban could trample Nirgand at such a speed in this world.
If not for Siron, Ban, and the Genesis knight like Jin and Luna.
Nirgand would have the power to end the world anytime. Without Genesis, nothing can fundamentally harm the Black Sea Five Kings.
[Ban, what do you intend to become? What do you want to be with such power?]
“It's a misconception I've had for a long time. I thought I was fighting for the survival and prosperity of the Plutonian. That was all I believed.”
Nirgand, struck by the Battle God's will, and the hundreds of thousands of real thunder pouring behind it.

The black land of the Black Sea, stained with spirit energy, was nowhere to be found on the battlefield. The blue lightning emitted by Ban and Nirgand's Sun energy constantly collided, creating white shockwaves.
[But?]
“Now, it's the same reason I'm here to cut you down. My power exists for Brother Jin.”
[Jin Runkandel... you're talking about Siron's son.]
“That's right.”
When Ban said 'we', it didn’t just include the Plutonian.

“Me and my brothers, and not just beings who happen to have a lot of power like you. We were monsters from the start, or eventually had to become monsters. Like you and my foolish ancestor who gave you that power.”
Sharp golden shards poured from Nirgand's wings, attacking Ban. It was the first time Nirgand successfully counterattacked.
The shards caused scratches all over Ban's body, but none penetrated deeply. Just a few droplets of blood were all.
“However, Brother Jin is different. Brother will do something unprecedented in the world.”
[What exactly is that?]
“I don't know precisely. I just feel it. Only Brother Jin can do it. Something like, saving the world. I'm just a sword for that purpose.”
[Salvation? That's abstract. Can you tell me more concretely?]
It wasn't mockery. Nirgand was genuinely curious. He wanted to understand why such a significant figure as Ban had chosen Jin Runkandel.
Even before Ban mentioned Jin, Nirgand had thought about him several times. After all, Jin was the one who killed his brother Gliac and the human most often mentioned by Siron.

Unlike Gliac, the Five Kings of the Black Sea, who were always present there, had tried time and again to infiltrate Siron's inner thoughts. Naturally, Nirgand had tormented Siron in this way dozens of times, and within Siron's mind were many thoughts related to Jin.
Thinking back now, it seemed that Siron also viewed Jin with a similar perspective as Ban.

"You, Nirgand, would not wish for a world where things disappear at someone's whim. In such a world, even battles like this would lose all meaning. If the power-holder decides they don't want your life, they could just erase it."
[Such power doesn't exist. You must be talking about the Ziffle, but they will fail. Especially if you are against them, there seems to be no small chance.]
"It exists. And while I might indeed be the strongest person in the world, I can't stop that power. That role is only for Brother Jin."
[Fate, is it…]
Ban actually felt that way. He could sense a massive, indescribable fate that looked only towards Jin.
At that moment, Nirgand suddenly looked up at the sky, startled.
He had accepted his imminent death, but he had no intention of fighting half-heartedly. Still, the reason Nirgand looked up was that he felt a gaze.
It was the gaze of the witch, spying on him and Ban. It was the first time, as far as Nirgand knew, that the witch had shown such disturbance.
Unlike Nirgand, Ban did not feel the witch's gaze. She simply guessed that there must be a reason for Nirgand's sudden behavior.
‘If I can't feel it, but Nirgand can, it must be something closely related to the spirit. Then it must be the witch.’
It wasn’t the first time the witch had spied on her. Unlike now, she had even come to Lafrarosa to meet Ban. In fact, Ban was probably the person the witch had observed the most so far.
Ban continued the battle undisturbed.

Right after a storm of fragments passed, Sigmund stretched out like light. Ban closed the distance to Nirgand in an instant, and his blade was already touching Nirgand's heart, the fragment of the Sun God.
The moment the blade and the fragment touched, an explosion sounded. For Ban, it was a rare moment of not being able to slice through with one strike.
The recoil sent Ban briefly into the air. Nirgand, screaming wildly, shot golden horns at her. Golden rays also burst from his eyes.
Ban didn't avoid them, descending straight towards and unfolding a slash at the fragment of the sun. Unblocked shards of the horn deeply pierced Ban's collarbone, waist, and thigh.
But these injuries were just a choice made to attack the fragment more effectively. The second strike was a determined one to cut through.
‘To prevent even a bit of Nirgand's power from leaking outside the Black Sea, now is the right time.’
In the brief moment Ban fell, the lightning energy that covered the entire battlefield condensed into Sigmund. Thus, the landscape around became entirely golden in an instant.
Ban and Nirgand both sensed that the fight was coming to an end. The Sun energy was engulfing Ban, but her descent speed did not decrease at all.
The blue blade split Nirgand's head.
It then crashed unhesitatingly into the fragment of the Sun God. The fragment released all the Sun energy it contained before the blade touched, but unlike the first time, Ban was not repelled.
Squeak…!
Ban felt a dull sensation on the blade as if it caught on bone, but it was brief. Sigmund then sliced through the fragment of the Sun God, falling to the ground.
As the fragment that had been radiating golden light was sliced, Nirgand's spirit began to pour out.
Nirgand's body did not recover anymore. Particles of spirit and Sun energy scattered in all directions.
“Huff…”

Ban steadied her breath and looked down at Nirgand's giant eye on the ground. The eye held curiosity, not anger or sorrow. Curiosity about what Jin Runkandel was, that someone like her had decided to exist solely for him.
The eye soon crumbled like a heap of dried sand. Nirgand met his end without knowing the answer.
The lightning energy of the Battle Kings spread across the sky, preventing the spirit and Sun energy radiating from Nirgand's corpse from spreading outward.
‘The energy is larger than I expected. Cleaning up will take a bit more effort…’
As Ban thought this, she slowly turned her head beyond Nirgand's corpse. Far away, she felt a very familiar yet new energy where Nirgand had last used the dimensional gate.
It was Siron's energy.
